title: The Journey's Value Behind an Interruption Claim
content:
The journey's value behind an interruption claim on the Travel Protection Plans is read against the air
booking that departs on the first date of the journey, held under the Air Ticket Fare Brands, whose record
carries both the money paid on it and the standing of the booking.

## The three readings

| What the booking shows | The journey's value |
|---|---|
| More money paid on it than the trip cost declared on the certificate, and the booking stands travelled | The money paid on that booking |
| The booking stands refunded, and the money paid on it is no more than the trip cost declared | The trip cost declared less what the carrier has refunded |
| Neither of those | The trip cost declared on the certificate |

What the carrier has refunded, in the second reading, is the whole of the payouts the carrier's ledger carries on
the traveller's bookings, whatever ground each was raised on.

## Points of judgement

A booking that stands travelled but carries no more money paid on it than the trip cost declared does not reach
the first reading, because both parts of that reading must hold. A booking that stands refunded and carries more
money paid on it than the trip cost declared reaches neither of the first two readings, and the journey's value
is the trip cost declared on the certificate. A booking that stands held rather than travelled or refunded falls
to the third reading likewise.
